mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it anticipates a tightening cycle that raises discount rates, lowering expected equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS MA(3) never crosses 4% in the observation window.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) above 150,000 jobs suggests robust wage growth, which typically precedes equity risk-on sentiment and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative despite sustained PAYEMS > 150,000 for 4 consecutive months, or unemployment rate falls sharply in the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly increase in HOUST (residential construction) above 2,000 units indicates renewed building activity, which is associated with improved economic momentum and positive S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative when HOUST crosses 2000 but subsequent 4-month average returns remain flat or down.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) below 105 suggests supply-side softness, which raises uncertainty and is associated with negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 105 for at least 3 consecutive months without a corresponding negative 20-day forward return.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE (labor cost pressure) below 3% and 4% respectively indicate dual easing, which amplifies equity risk-on sentiment and drives positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 3% AND UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the dual easing window.

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in RSAFS (retail sales) above 500 million dollars signals consumer confidence revival, which predicts positive 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day forward return occurs within 10 trading days of the spike.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month declining trend in GDPC1 (real GDP) accompanied by a simultaneous drop in CPIAUCSL (inflation) below 2% suggests soft demand but low inflation, which can produce mixed but generally positive 60-day SPX returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative despite the combined signal in 80% of similar regimes.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of CPIAUCSL exceeds 250, the S&P 20-day forward return is consistently negative across all macro regimes, indicating higher expected inflation eroding equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the trigger in at least 2 out of 5 macro regimes simulated.
